TV PANEL DEFECT & DAMAGE POLICY (rev. 4)
1. Standard warranty: any television with 5 or more dead or stuck pixels found within 90 days of delivery qualifies for a free replacement panel or unit, no deductible.
2. After 90 days from delivery, dead-pixel claims are not covered under the standard warranty regardless of pixel count.
3. Extended Care Plan (if purchased at checkout): extends dead-pixel coverage to 365 days from delivery, subject to the same 5-pixel threshold, no deductible. The Extended Care Plan does NOT cover cosmetic scratches or user-caused cracks.
4. Accidental damage (drops, cracks) is covered only under the separate Accidental Damage Add-on, subject to a $150 deductible, maximum 2 claims per year.
5. Priority order: if a unit qualifies under both the standard warranty and the Extended Care Plan, apply the standard warranty first (no deductible either way, but avoids drawing down the Extended Care claim count).
6. Registration requirement: the Extended Care Plan is only active if the customer registers the plan within 14 days of the delivery date, via the online portal or by calling support. Claims filed under an unregistered Extended Care Plan are treated as if no Extended Care Plan had been purchased at all.

CASE FILE
Customer: Bram Voss
Product: Nexoria 55in OLED
Purchase date: Jan 3
Delivery date: Jan 10
Extended Care Plan: purchased at checkout, registered online on Jan 12
Accidental Damage Add-on: not purchased
Today's date: Apr 20 (100 days after delivery)
Reported issue: 6 dead pixels clustered in the lower-left corner. No drops, cracks, or physical damage reported or observed by the technician.

Technician visit note, Apr 18: Confirmed 6 dead/stuck pixels in the lower-left quadrant using a full-screen color test pattern. Panel otherwise structurally intact; no cracks, dents, or liquid ingress observed. Customer stated the pixels appeared gradually over the past two weeks, not from a single incident.

Customer's original complaint, submitted via the support portal on Apr 19: "I've noticed a cluster of dead pixels on my TV, seems to have appeared over the last couple of weeks. This is my first time dealing with this, what are my options? I did buy the Extended Care add-on so I'm hoping that's still valid even though it's past the 3-month mark."

Claim reference: WC-2291. Logged by Support Agent Priya N. Escalation required: no, standard Extended Care workflow applies. Customer account notes: this is the first warranty claim on file for this account, with no prior claims history.

FORMAL NOTICE OF DEFECTIVE GOODS

Date: 14 March
To: Clarion Retail Customer Rights Department
Re: Order #CR-40218, Clarion Vista 27in Monitor. Purchased 24 February for $612.00 including tax via credit card; delivered 1 March; invoice #INV-77821.

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing pursuant to Section 54 of the Consumer Guarantees Act regarding the above order. Upon unboxing on 1 March, the monitor's screen was found to be cracked across the lower third. The shipping carton and internal foam packaging showed no dents, tears, or signs of impact, which indicates the panel most likely left the factory already cracked rather than being damaged in transit.

This is my second attempt to raise this matter. I first called your support line on 4 March (reference CS-88213) and was told a case manager would call back within 48 hours; no call was received. I called again on 9 March and was told the case had been closed in error without ever contacting me.

For the avoidance of doubt, I have attached to this letter (Appendix A) four photographs of the crack taken in natural light, along with a photograph of the intact packaging materials referenced above. I also took the unit to an independent repair shop, GreenTech Repairs, on 6 March for a second opinion; their technician, without prompting, independently concluded the crack pattern was consistent with a factory-applied panel defect rather than an impact fracture.

For context, this is the second Clarion product I have purchased this year; the first, a Clarion SoundBar Mini, has performed without any issues, so I do not believe I am simply having bad luck with this brand.

I request a full replacement unit under Section 54(2) of the Act. I am not seeking a monetary refund at this time, as I would like to continue using this monitor model. Under Section 55 of the Act, retailers are required to substantively respond to a written defect notice within 10 business days of receipt; I therefore expect a response by 28 March. If the matter remains unresolved by that date, I will file a complaint with the Consumer Disputes Tribunal and will seek reimbursement of my call costs in addition to the replacement.

Please advise on return logistics for the defective unit at your earliest convenience. This letter is sent without prejudice to any other statutory rights I may have.

Regards,
Elena Kovac

CC: Consumer Rights Advocacy Group (information only)
Enclosures: Appendix A (four photographs), GreenTech Repairs assessment note
